overview_page.body:
Reasoning Odyssey Gate -- Week 10 -- Honest Visualization from Project Data (S09/S06/S08)

What are we learning? Honest data visualization -- choosing a defensible representation and naming what it could mislead someone into believing.

What am I building/changing? State a real question about your own selected-world/project data. Produce one or more readable, labeled visualizations that answer it, explain why the representation is defensible, and identify one misleading alternative or visual pitfall. Retain runnable code/data or a reproducible trace -- plotting syntax alone is not the evidence.

How does my world connect? This uses your own accumulated project data -- the same system you have been building since Week 3.

What evidence do I keep? Keep one concise World Bible entry: what changed, evidence used, and any remaining debt.

Success criteria (25 points)

CriterionPointsMeets expectation
Real question / labeled visualization8A genuine question about the student own data, answered with a readable, labeled chart.
Reproducible evidence7Runnable code/data or a reproducible trace is retained, not just an image.
Representation/pitfall reasoning / World Bible6Explains why the representation is defensible and names one pitfall.
AI accountability4When AI was used: proposal, diff, independent test, reasoning, accept/reject decision.

What exactly do I turn in? The graded Canvas assignment for this gate is now live -- find it in this module, in Assignments, or in Grades, and submit there using the submission types and rubric described above.

What carries forward? Week 11 either extends this data story or, if the project is not yet data-rich, reinforces prior design/GUI/testing work instead.
